findings.title: Automatic count distractors lack opening math delimiter and every valid finite collection is rejected
findings.evidence: valid-five-auto throws; domain4/domain20 throw; actual generator seeds1..64 all64 fail. Valid caller-supplied four distractors succeed.
findings.cause: Array.from callback builds `${n}$개`, which fails readCount /^\$(0|[1-9]\d*)\$개$/. The correct answer cannot be removed from that malformed pool either.
findings.impact: Advertised automatic finite-domain multiple-choice derivation is unavailable for supported classification tasks; fail-closed, not a mathematical false approval.
findings.recommendation: Construct the same canonical $n$개 representation as readCount accepts; rerun direct N4/N20 and actual64 generator successes plus negative controls. Parent must implement separately.

findings.title: Collection recognizer treats ellipsis and blank math rows as explicit members
findings.evidence: A final $\cdots$ or $ $ row returns bound5 and accepts valid in-range authored distractors; whitespace-distinct duplicate $ x=x $ also evades the raw duplicate guard.
findings.impact: A syntactically dollar-wrapped list is not necessarily the complete explicit collection promised by the function. Ellipsis makes total population unknown; blank row is not a printed expression. Numeric bound is unsupported in these adversarial cases.
findings.recommendation: Conservatively decline empty/whitespace/ellipsis placeholders and normalize only safe presentation whitespace before duplicate checking, or narrow/document supported list grammar. Do not add symbolic equivalence or grading approval.

countChecks.unsupportedSemantics: This branch bounds numeric choices only. It does not prove which expressions are equations/linear equations, correct answer truth, distractor pedagogy, target grade or rights.

overall: summarizer correction supported; finite count branch has blocking implementation defect and incomplete-collection guard findings
